milestones.title: Foundations & Schema Modeling
milestones.subtitle: From Raw SQL to Relational Schemas
milestones.description: Master the database problems ORMs solve, Prisma v7 setup, declarative schema design, native types, constraints, and all relational patterns (1:1, 1:N, M:N).

milestones.title: Migrations, Operations & Controlled Reads
milestones.subtitle: Database Evolution & Optimized Querying
milestones.description: Safely evolve schemas with migrations and seeders, manage connection pools and client singletons, and build precise read queries with select, include, filters, and pagination.

milestones.title: Mutations, Data Integrity & Transactions
milestones.subtitle: ACID Guarantees & Safe Writes
milestones.description: Safely accept user input with Zod, execute atomic updates and idempotent upserts, configure referential cascade actions, and master nested writes with ACID transactions.

milestones.title: Production REST APIs & Resilience
milestones.subtitle: Enterprise Architecture & Hardening
milestones.description: Intercept Prisma error codes without leaking database internals, build robust Express error middleware, and architect a complete production-grade publishing REST API.

days.title: Day 1 — Why Prisma?
days.description: Learn why traditional raw SQL drivers leave your TypeScript code vulnerable to silent runtime bugs, and how Prisma generates a fully type-safe, auto-completing database client directly from your schema.
completionLearnings: Understand the Object-Relational Impedance Mismatch and why raw SQL strings are invisible to the TypeScript compiler
Learn how Prisma Client dynamically infers TypeScript return types directly from your query parameters
Use findUnique and select to fetch lean, targeted records without over-fetching database columns
Understand the three architectural pillars: schema.prisma, Prisma Client, and Prisma Migrate

concepts.title: The Type-Safety Gap: Why Raw SQL Fails TypeScript
concepts.shortDescription: Why raw SQL strings leave your backend blind to typos and schema changes, and how Prisma gives your database queries real compile-time guarantees.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Read and Shape a Record by Primary Key
instructions: Pass where: { id: userId } to target the primary key
Use select: { id: true, name: true } so only id and name are retrieved

tasks.title: Task 2 (Guided): Query by Unique Constraint (Email Lookup)
instructions: Pass where: { email } to filter by the unique email address
Select id, name, and email in the response

tasks.title: Task 3 (Independent): Eliminate Type Bypasses ("as any")
instructions: Remove "as any" completely from the query
Replace the invalid field user_mail with the schema-defined email field
Select id and email in the returned record

concepts.title: Lean Projections: Why SELECT * Hurts Production Apps
concepts.shortDescription: Why fetching entire database rows degrades performance, and how Prisma select shapes both network payloads and TypeScript types.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Query a Student Directory with Lean Projection
instructions: Use select: { name: true, department: true }
Do not fetch unused columns like id, age, or city

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Build a Safe User Profile Card
instructions: Select only name and email in the return payload

concepts.title: The Prisma Triad: Schema, Client, and Migrate
concepts.shortDescription: How schema.prisma, Prisma Client, and Prisma Migrate coordinate to keep your database, SQL migrations, and TypeScript types in perfect sync.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Query Auth Credentials with Precision
instructions: Call prisma.user.findUnique with where: { id: userId }
Select only id: true and email: true

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Query with Schema-Defined Unique Constraint
instructions: Select only id, name, and email

finalChallenge.title: Day 1 Challenge: The Production API Refactor
finalChallenge.scenario: Your backend engineering team is deprecating an old Express microservice that relied on fragile, untyped raw SQL strings. You are tasked with replacing the legacy lookup query with a type-safe Prisma query that fetches an active user by email and projects only their id, name, and email fields.

tasks.title: Replace Legacy Raw SQL with Typed Prisma Query
instructions: Select only id, name, and email
Do not use raw SQL strings or "as any" type assertions

days.title: Day 2 — Modern Prisma Setup & Configuration
days.description: Master datasource configuration, configure connection pooling for serverless and cloud PostgreSQL, and bridge legacy SQL snake_case tables to idiomatic TypeScript camelCase using @map and @@map.
completionLearnings: Understand datasource and client generator declarations in schema.prisma
Configure connection pooling parameters for serverless environments (PgBouncer, Neon, Supabase)
Map legacy snake_case database tables and columns to clean TypeScript camelCase models without altering live database tables

concepts.title: Datasource Architecture & Connection Pooling in Cloud Backends
concepts.shortDescription: How Prisma connects to PostgreSQL, and why serverless environments require connection poolers to prevent database connection exhaustion.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Configure PostgreSQL Datasource & Generator
instructions: Define datasource db with provider = "postgresql" and url = env("DATABASE_URL")

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Append Connection Pooling Parameters
instructions: Use the standard URL object to parse basePostgresUrl

concepts.title: The Naming Bridge: Mapping snake_case SQL to camelCase TypeScript
concepts.shortDescription: How to use @map and @@map to write clean, idiomatic TypeScript while preserving legacy database table and column names.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Map Customer Model and Email Column
instructions: Add @@map("tbl_customers") at the bottom of model Customer

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Map Phone & Registered Date Columns

finalChallenge.title: Day 2 Challenge: Modernize an Introspected Auth Schema
finalChallenge.scenario: Your engineering team used "prisma db pull" to introspect an existing legacy PostgreSQL database. The generated model uses raw snake_case table and column names. Clean up the AuthUser model so developers use clean camelCase properties while the database keeps its exact snake_case columns intact.

tasks.title: Map AuthUser Model and Columns
instructions: Define model AuthUser with id Int @id @default(autoincrement())

days.title: Day 3 — Models, Fields, Enums & Constraints
days.description: Design production-grade database schemas: choose appropriate scalar types, handle financial precision with Decimal, enforce valid domain values with Enums, and guarantee integrity with composite unique constraints.
completionLearnings: Understand why JavaScript floating-point numbers break financial math and why Prisma Decimal is required
Model optional fields (?) vs required fields and use @updatedAt for automated audit timestamps
Declare native PostgreSQL Enums and configure default values
Enforce multi-column uniqueness using composite constraints like @@unique([studentId, courseId])

concepts.title: Scalar Types, Nullability & The Precision Problem
concepts.shortDescription: Why floating-point numbers corrupt financial data, how cuid() provides distributed IDs, and how nullability works in schema.prisma.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Create Product Model with Precision Types
Task 2 (Independent): Create Article Model with Unique Slug

concepts.title: Enforcing Invariants: Enums & Multi-Field Constraints
concepts.shortDescription: How Enums eliminate arbitrary string bugs, and how composite constraints (@@unique, @@id) prevent duplicate data in relational tables.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Define OrderStatus Enum & Order Model
instructions: Define enum OrderStatus with the 5 statuses
Model Order with id Int @id @default(autoincrement()), status OrderStatus @default(PENDING), and total Decimal

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Add Composite Unique Constraint to Enrollment

finalChallenge.title: Day 3 Challenge: Design an E-Commerce Favorites System
finalChallenge.scenario: Your e-commerce platform needs a favorites system where users can favorite products. A user can favorite multiple products, and a product can be favorited by multiple users. Design a UserFavorite join model with composite primary key @@id([userId, productId]).

tasks.title: Design UserFavorite Composite Model
instructions: Add userId Int and productId Int

days.title: Day 4 — Relational Schema Modeling (1:1, 1:N, M:N)
days.description: Master relational modeling in Prisma: understand how foreign keys connect tables, why scalar fields differ from relation fields, enforce 1:1 uniqueness, and model explicit many-to-many join tables.
completionLearnings: Differentiate physical foreign key columns (authorId Int) from virtual TypeScript relation fields (author User)
Understand why 1-to-1 relations require @unique on the foreign key to avoid accidentally creating a 1-to-Many relation
Model optional relations using nullable foreign keys (Int?)
Compare Prisma implicit many-to-many relations with explicit join models

concepts.title: One-to-Many (1:N): Scalar Columns vs Virtual Relation Fields
concepts.shortDescription: How foreign keys link tables, and why Prisma cleanly separates the SQL column from the TypeScript navigation property.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Connect Author and Book (1:N)
instructions: In model Book, add authorId Int

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Optional 1:N Relation (Company & Employee)
instructions: In model Employee, add companyId Int?

concepts.title: One-to-One (1:1): The @unique Mandate
concepts.shortDescription: Why omitting @unique on a foreign key accidentally creates a 1:Many relation, and how 1:1 relations enforce strict pairing.

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Fix 1:1 Unique Constraint Bug
instructions: Add @unique to driverId in model License

finalChallenge.title: Day 4 Challenge: Model a Hospital Doctor-Patient Relational Graph
finalChallenge.scenario: A healthcare SaaS platform needs relational models for Doctor and Appointment. A Doctor has many Appointments, and an Appointment belongs to exactly one Doctor. Model this 1-to-Many relationship with proper foreign keys.

tasks.title: Model Doctor-Appointment 1:N Relationship
instructions: In model Doctor, add appointments Appointment[]
In model Appointment, add doctorId Int
In model Appointment, add doctor Doctor @relation(fields: [doctorId], references: [id])

days.title: Errors + Express Error Middleware
days.description: Intercept Prisma error codes (P2002, P2025), prevent leaking database internals, and build clean Express HTTP error middleware.
completionLearnings: Identified critical Prisma error codes: P2002 (unique constraint violation), P2025 (record not found), and P2003 (foreign key failure)
Built centralized Express error middleware mapping database errors to clean HTTP 409, 404, and 400 status responses
Hardened production APIs to prevent sensitive stack traces and SQL queries leaking to clients

concepts.title: Prisma Error Classification & Error Codes
concepts.shortDescription: Catch Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError and inspect typed error codes.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Intercept P2002 Duplicate Email Error
Task 2 (Independent): Catch P2025 Record Not Found on Delete
instructions: Catch P2025 error and return { error: "Post not found" }

concepts.title: Centralized Express Error Middleware
concepts.shortDescription: Decouple route controllers from error formatting with centralized Express middleware.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Express Error Handler for P2002 and P2025
instructions: If err.code === "P2002", return res.status(409).json({ error: "Resource already exists" })
If err.code === "P2025", return res.status(404).json({ error: "Resource not found" })
Default to res.status(500).json({ error: "Internal server error" })

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Extend Middleware with Zod 400 Validation
instructions: Check if err.name === "ZodError" or err instanceof ZodError
Return res.status(400).json({ error: "Validation Error", issues: err.issues })

tasks.title: Step 1: Harden User Creation Against Duplicates
